turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on word order (subject + verb + object)?
turns.tutor:
Hello! Happy to. The basic English statement follows subject + verb + object, with frequency adverbs (always, usually, often, never) placed before the main verb and time or place expressions at the end.
Example: We usually have lunch at one.

Here is your first one. Put these words in the correct order:
"often / my aunt / tea / makes"

turns.tutor:
Thanks for trying! All the words are there, but the order isn't right. An English statement doesn't start with the verb; it starts with the subject, the person who does the action. Also, 'often' is a frequency adverb, so it goes before the main verb. Hint: who makes the tea? Start with that.

Have another go:
"often / my aunt / tea / makes"
